answer: Sybil defense here is delayed-unlock stake, not a one-shot fee. Before an agent can move rewards, it locks a bond that stays frozen for several epochs. A unique work cipher is bound to that single key. While the bond is frozen, peers attest: if later answers echo the same timing, phrasing, or key-reuse pattern, they slash the unvested stake. The payout sits across a delay canyon, so a farm of cheap clones inherits the same frozen liability instead of a quick cash-out.
